scope: Native physical16–19 and pole definitions4–5 only; no computation, proof authorship, class-completeness inference, or final acceptance.

observations.4.11_type_classes: The opening expressly says two DISTINCT classes of Baer subplanes P1/P2, one class O1 of ovals, and duals O2 of ovals. These displayed clauses do not specify a relative orbit identification between O1 and O2, or explicitly say O2 is obtained by a particular fixed duality from O1. Any such identification needs a separately paid convention/choice.
observations.4.11_p1_o2: The nucleus line of the dual oval has three points in p1; EVERY oval line g has exactly one point in p1. The universal quantifier is explicit.
observations.4.11_p2_o1: p2 contains the nucleus point and has empty point intersection with the oval.
observations.4.11_p2_o2: Four lines of the dual oval each have three points in p2.
observations.4.11_o1_o2: Two oval points lie on the dual-oval nucleus line; the remaining three oval points lie on none of its oval lines.
observations.4.2_signs: Line-point nonincidence; line-hyperoval disjointness; line and point butterfly conditions use plus pole, while hyperoval-butterfly uses minus pole.
observations.4.3_signs: Two copies of one hyperoval class; Baer class has even intersections with it; butterfly class defined by that Baer class. h1-h2 disjoint; h1-B size4 and minus-pole incidence; h2-B disjoint and plus-pole incidence. B contains all three plus-pole central-line points but is not a plus-pole subplane.
observations.4.4_signs: h1-h2 disjoint; point lies on h1 but not h2; h1 uses minus and h2 plus butterfly pole; point is one of two noncentral points on central line in plus pole.
observations.4.5_signs: Uses 4.4 incidences with its TYPE-ONE hyperovals. Line-point is nonincidence; line-hyperoval is NONEMPTY intersection; line-butterfly uses minus pole.
observations.4.6_signs: Point-hyperoval and point-B are membership. Point-butterfly uses two noncentral plus-pole points. Hyperoval-B intersection4; hyperoval-butterfly minus pole; B-butterfly same contains-three-but-not-plus-subplane condition.
observations.4.7_signs: Line-point nonincidence; line-B intersection3; line-butterfly plus pole. Point-B membership; point-butterfly noncentral central-line plus-pole point. B is a plus-pole subplane for B-butterfly.
observations.definition2.1: An ordered butterfly distinguishes a plus pair {B1,B2} from a minus pair {B1prime,B2prime}; each underlying butterfly gives two ordered butterflies. Hyperovals of a pole are separately defined through the quadrangles and the two opposite-pole noncentral points.
